extracted.intended_audience: Members of the Patent Trial and Appeal Board; patent practitioners and parties in AIA post-grant proceedings (IPR/PGR) with parallel district court or ITC litigation
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for the Board's exercise of discretion to deny institution of IPRs/PGRs where there is parallel district court or ITC litigation, including how to apply Fintiv and related precedent and which evidence or stipulations will be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of rescission / applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: The rescission applies to any case in which the Board has not issued an institution decision, or where a request for rehearing or Director Review of an institution decision was filed and remains pending.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Board will consider timely requests for additional briefing on the application of the Interim Procedure's rescission on a case-by-case basis. Absent extraordinary circumstances, the Board will not revisit a decision on institution if the time for seeking Director Review or rehearing has passed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply Fintiv factors to parallel ITC proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board will apply the Fintiv factors when there is a parallel proceeding at the International Trade Commission (ITC).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although an ITC final invalidity determination does not have preclusive effect, it is difficult as a practical matter to assert patent claims that the ITC has determined are invalid. Instituting an IPR/PGR where the ITC has set a target date for completing its investigation earlier than the Board's deadline to issue a final written decision may increase duplication and expenses, making denial more likely. Conversely, the Board is less likely to deny institution under Fintiv where the ITC projected final determination date is after the Board's deadline to issue a final written decision. (See Fintiv, Paper 11 at 8-9.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of timely Sotera stipulations
rubrics_metrics.description: A timely-filed Sotera stipulation (a petitioner stipulating that, if an IPR/PGR is instituted, the petitioner will not pursue in district court or in the ITC any ground raised or that could have been reasonably raised in the IPR/PGR) is highly relevant but not dispositive by itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such a stipulation will be considered as part of the Board's holistic analysis under Fintiv. Note the precedent in NXP USA, Inc. v. Impinj, Inc. (IPR2021-01556, Paper 13) that the only appropriate time for a petitioner to offer a stipulation is prior to the Board's decision on institution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of evidence about timing/proximity of parallel proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board may consider any evidence that the parties make of record that bears on the proximity of the district court's trial date or the ITC's final determination target date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relevant evidence may include median time-to-trial statistics for civil actions in the district court in which the parallel litigation resides, or other record evidence that informs whether the parallel tribunal will reach a final determination before the Board's deadline to issue a final written decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balanced assessment of Fintiv factors including merits
rubrics_metrics.description: The factors considered in the exercise of discretion are part of a balanced assessment of all the relevant circumstances in the case, including the strength of the merits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While the strength of the merits is a component of the holistic analysis, compelling merits alone is not dispositive in making the discretionary assessment under Fintiv.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restoration to prior precedent (Fintiv and Sotera) in absence of rulemaking
rubrics_metrics.description: With rescission of the Interim Procedure, policy reverts to the guidance in place before the Interim Procedure, including the Board's precedential decisions in Fintiv and Sotera.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Interim Procedure was intended as temporary guidance pending potential rulemaking; because the USPTO did not subsequently propose a final rule addressing discretionary institution in view of parallel litigation, the Interim Procedure was rescinded and prior precedential guidance (Fintiv, Sotera) governs unless and until changed by rule or further precedent.
